clue.text: Fail to avoid young lady

blocks.note: first meaning: to fail to hit or to escape something, as in ... the target, or to steer clear of it
second meaning: the title for an unmarried young woman

explanation.walkthrough: The word packs two senses into the first phrase: fail (to hit) and avoid (as in narrowly missing the traffic). The last two words are the courtesy title.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both failing to hit and dodging, while the noun is the polite title for an unmarried girl.

clue.text: Leader of military junta shot head of charging animal

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front
something shot is wrecked or ruined, so the letters are knocked out of order
the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of military
taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the first letter of charging

explanation.surface: A rebel commander gunned down a charging beast at the head of a military junta.
explanation.walkthrough: The military junta and its shot leader suggest a coup, but 'shot' just scrambles the word junta.
explanation.definitionFit: The muntjac is a small Asian deer, also called the barking deer, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: They provide traction, as shown in broadcast about foremost of cars

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
about means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
the foremost part of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the first letter of cars

explanation.surface: A TV programme on cars demonstrates something that gives tyres grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as a TV programme, but it scrambles the three words before it, which then wrap around the C from cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow chains are fitted around tyres to give grip on icy or snowy roads, which is traction.

clue.text: Mount unlikely check, about work of little value

indicators.note: an unlikely version of a word is an improbable, distorted one, so its letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
ch. is the chess notation for check
c. is short for circa, Latin for about
op. is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: An improbable inspection is staged around a job that is barely worth doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not much cop' is British slang for poor or worthless; 'cop' here means value, not a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something mediocre or disappointing, worth very little.

clue.text: Clear above top of tower

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

blocks.note: over is a synonym for above
the first letter of tower

explanation.surface: Something is visible high over the summit of a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means plainly visible and open, so clear in the sense of obvious.

clue.text: One keeping score by enclosure with a felt-tip

blocks.note: a marker records points in a game
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A scorekeeper stands by a paddock, holding a felt-tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A marker pen is a thick-nibbed pen with a felt point, so the felt-tip is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Accepted the law needs changing in a protectorate

indicators.note: changing a word alters it, so its letters are set in a different order

blocks.note: common, as in common knowledge, means generally accepted
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal reform is required in a territory under another state's protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is historical: England's republic of 1649 to 1660 was the Commonwealth, and its later years under Cromwell were the Protectorate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Commonwealth and the Protectorate both name Cromwell's republican government, so one stands for the other.

clue.text: Mould in shed

blocks.note: first meaning: a shaped form for molten metal or plaster
second meaning: to throw off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests fungus growing in a garden shed, but shed is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is a mould or the object shaped in one, and to cast is to discard skin or feathers.

clue.text: Evergreen, over in glen, I pollarded

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the letters run back the other way
in says the letters sit inside the following words, spanning their boundary

blocks.note: the letters running across the end of glen, the I and the start of pollarded

explanation.surface: A woodsman cut back an evergreen tree down in the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Pollarded is a tree-cutting word that fits the surface, but its first letter is just part of the concealed string.
explanation.definitionFit: A pine is a coniferous tree that keeps its needles all year, an example of an evergreen.

clue.text: Name one volatile gas

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and liable to change, so the letters do not stay put

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Identify a single gas that evaporates readily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volatile gas' reads as a chemistry phrase, but volatile works on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble element that exists as an inert gas, used in glowing signs.

clue.text: TV lawyer, character defending army suspect

indicators.note: to defend something is to shield it, so one piece wraps protectively around another
a suspect version is dubious and not to be trusted as written, so its letters get rearranged

blocks.note: a character in a story is a person
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A television attorney, a character in a drama, defends a soldier accused of a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom picture fits the answer perfectly, which is why 'defending' and 'suspect' are so easy to read as plot rather than instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Perry Mason is Erle Stanley Gardner's fictional defence attorney, famous from the long-running American television series.

clue.text: The enemy is bound to take its toll? Wait and see

blocks.note: from the saying that time is the enemy
will expresses certainty about the future
to tell on someone is to have a marked, wearing effect

explanation.surface: Ageing will inevitably wear us down, so be patient and find out.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay half reads as a single proverb about age, which hides that it splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the truth will emerge in due course, so one should be patient and see.

clue.text: Provider of childish amusement, card giving evidence?

blocks.note: the jack is a court card in a pack
a witness gives evidence from the witness box

explanation.surface: A toy entertains children; a joker turns witness in court.
explanation.walkthrough: In British courts a witness stands in the witness box, so 'in the box' means testifying.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-in-the-box is a toy figure on a spring that leaps out of a box, delighting small children.

clue.text: Book desolate inn

blocks.note: bleak means bare and desolate
a public house is an inn

explanation.surface: Reserve a room at a gloomy, isolated hostelry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb about reserving a room, but it is a noun naming the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak House is a novel by Charles Dickens, so the answer is an example of a book.

clue.text: Drink from trophy after Cambridge college lost at last

indicators.note: after says the piece named before it is placed second, following the college and its letter
at last points to the final letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: Clare is a college of Cambridge University
the last letter of lost
a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: A rowing crew drinks from the cup after their college lost the final race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the trophy word after the college and its added letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret cup is an iced punch made with red Bordeaux wine, fruit and soda, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Tell all to move nearer fair

blocks.note: to come is to approach
a clean fight is a fair one

explanation.surface: A confessor is urged to step closer to a fairground.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is an idiom for confessing everything, revealing the whole truth.

clue.text: Fortunate? Very possibly

blocks.note: first meaning: as in 'it is just as ...', meaning lucky or fitting
second meaning: as in 'it may ... rain', meaning quite likely

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes it sound like a doubtful reply about luck; both halves are separate senses of one adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'just as well' the word means lucky, and in 'may well' it adds strong probability.

clue.text: Opposed to some in Constantinople

indicators.note: some of a word is only a part of it, so the letters lie inside the next word

blocks.note: the letters in the middle of the old name of Istanbul

explanation.surface: Some citizens of the old Byzantine capital opposed something.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a preposition means against, so it substitutes for opposed to.

clue.text: Volunteers to feed US artist's fish

indicators.note: to feed something is to put food into it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Man Ray was an American surrealist artist and photographer
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Helpers turn up to give food to an American painter's fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive belongs to the artist; with the reserve force set inside it gives the plural fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Manta rays are huge plankton-eating rays, which are cartilaginous fish.

clue.text: Contemptible involving Church of England in witchcraft

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: a sorry state is a pitiful, contemptible one
CE is the abbreviation for Church of England

explanation.surface: A shameful scandal draws the established church into accusations of witchcraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is the use of magic powers, a synonym for witchcraft.

clue.text: One eager to leave bang on time caught guard breaking into cupboard

definitions.text: One eager to leave bang on time

indicators.note: something breaking into a place forces its way inside it

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a locker is a small lockable cupboard
to watch is to keep guard

explanation.surface: An escapee is caught as a guard breaks into a cupboard right on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The guard word goes between the two halves of the cupboard word, after the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock-watcher is an employee who keeps checking the time, impatient to finish work at the exact moment.

clue.text: Reportedly distraught playwright

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so it is the spoken sound that counts

blocks.note: wild means frantic or distraught

explanation.surface: A dramatist is said to be beside himself with worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde wrote The Importance of Being Earnest, so he is an example of a playwright.

clue.text: Broadcast about introduction of cigarette lighter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around another
the introduction of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering
the first letter of cigarette

explanation.surface: An advert promotes a new cigarette lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cigarette lighter' looks like one object, but lighter is the definition: a flat barge, not a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat for carrying cargo, the same sort of vessel as a lighter.

clue.text: A single person, out of condition, losing heart

indicators.note: losing its heart means a word drops its central letter

blocks.note: unfit means out of condition

explanation.surface: A lone individual who is out of shape is feeling discouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single individual counted as one whole, as in a family unit.

clue.text: Drudge recalled being beaten about at home

indicators.note: something beaten is battered out of shape, so its letters are scrambled
about means around, so the scrambled letters encircle the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A household servant remembers being beaten at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' tempts as a reversal signal, but here it is the fodder for the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella is the fairy-tale stepdaughter made to do the household chores, so her name means a drudge.

clue.text: First to recognise a French character

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the first letter of recognise
une is French for a, the feminine indefinite article

explanation.surface: Be the first to spot a French person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rune is a letter of the old Germanic alphabet, so it is a written character.

clue.text: Weak type, complete killjoy

blocks.note: a wet is British slang for a feeble, ineffectual person
blanket means total, as in blanket coverage

explanation.surface: A feeble person who is an utter spoilsport.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is an idiom for someone who dampens others' fun, exactly a killjoy.

clue.text: Extremely clever? Yes, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of clever and the start of yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a person is exceptionally clever and gets a partial yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Very is an intensifier meaning to a high degree, a synonym of extremely.
